## Inca Cueva in Argentina: Ancient Rock Art in the Gorges of Jujuy

Inca Cueva appeals to travelers interested in human history and Andean archaeology. This group of rock shelters is in the highlands of Jujuy province, surrounded by rocky ledges, red and ocher-colored cliffs, a dry streambed and images left by people long before the region's modern population.

The name might suggest that all the monuments date from the Inca Empire. In fact, the shelters were used much earlier. Archaeologists study different periods of human presence here, while the paintings reveal a portion of cultural heritage that has no surviving written records.

## What Has Survived in the Rock Shelters?

Inca Cueva is known for paintings on rock surfaces, including areas that researchers identify by the numbers assigned to individual caves and shelters. The paintings were made with mineral pigments and differ in subject matter and age. Their scientific value lies not only in individual figures but also in the positioning of images, the materials used for pigments, the condition of the rock faces and the archaeological context.

The government of Jujuy has reported a special archaeometric research program focused on Inca Cueva's rock paintings. Specialists examine pigment composition, painting methods, natural deterioration and the effects of visitors. This helps identify ways to preserve the images for future generations.

Visitors should know that not every surface may be approached freely, viewed at arm's length or photographed using flash. Access restrictions protect the fragile site and are set by the responsible custodians.

## Why the Gorge Matters for Understanding Archaeology

In Inca Cueva's natural setting, ancient shelters seem part of the mountain landscape itself. Reddish layered rocks, dry watercourses and overhanging stone ledges help explain why people might have chosen these spots for temporary habitation and other activities. Archaeological finds offer insights into life in high-altitude conditions as it changed over thousands of years.

The region is linked to the history of Andean peoples who existed long before the Spanish conquest. It is therefore important to distinguish museum accounts of the documented Inca era from research into much older archaeological remains. Inca Cueva offers a view of northern Argentina's longer history.

## Combining Inca Cueva with the Quebrada de Humahuaca

Many journeys through Jujuy province focus on the [Quebrada de Humahuaca](/argentina/place/quebrada-de-humahuaca/). This region includes [Purmamarca](/argentina/place/purmamarca/) with its Hill of Seven Colors, [Tilcara](/argentina/place/tilcara/) and its archaeological sites, [Uquía](/argentina/place/uquia/) and historic [Humahuaca](/argentina/place/humahuaca/).

| Stop | What to explore |
|---|---|
| [Purmamarca](/argentina/place/purmamarca/) | Colorful rock formations |
| [Tilcara](/argentina/place/tilcara/) | Settlements and archaeology |
| [Humahuaca](/argentina/place/humahuaca/) | History and local culture |
| Inca Cueva | Rock shelters and paintings |

These stops reveal different aspects of the same region. The Hill of Seven Colors is remarkable for its geology, Tilcara's monuments help explain settlement patterns, and Inca Cueva preserves much earlier evidence of life in the mountains.

## Is Inca Cueva Included in Ada Tours Journeys?

Our [15-day "Argentina: A Grand Journey from Iguazu to Patagonia" itinerary](/multi-country/tour/argentina-grand-tour-15-days/) devotes a day to the Quebrada de Humahuaca, including the Hill of Seven Colors, Tilcara, Uquía, Humahuaca and Inca Cueva. The route includes a Russian-speaking guide and an overnight stay near Purmamarca. The archaeological site is one element of a larger cultural and nature journey.

The exact duration and format of the visit depend on that day's program and the site's access rules. Having Inca Cueva on the stop list does not mean unrestricted access to every archaeological surface. If rock art is your main reason for traveling, discuss viewing arrangements separately from the gorge's other attractions.

## Preparing for the Trip and Visiting with Care

The highland setting calls for comfortable closed shoes, water, sun protection and clothing for wind. Paths near rocky areas may be quite different from well-maintained urban walkways. Check the length of the approach, which shelters are accessible and whether a local guide is required for your date.

Archaeological paintings are particularly vulnerable to touching, moisture, soot and unauthorized marks. Do not touch pigments or leave your own marks on the rock. The experience is more rewarding when time is divided between studying the paintings and observing the surrounding terrain.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Inca Cueva

### Was Inca Cueva created only during Inca times?

No. The shelters studied here record a much longer history of human presence in the region. The site's name does not determine the age of all its paintings.

### Can the paintings be seen without a guide?

Access depends on the particular area and current conservation rules. Find out in advance which shelters are open and whether guiding is required.

### Are Inca Cueva and the Hill of Seven Colors in the same place?

No. [Purmamarca](/argentina/place/purmamarca/) is known for its colorful hillsides, while Inca Cueva is an archaeological complex. A longer trip through Jujuy can include both on one regional itinerary.

### Is Inca Cueva suitable for a quick stop?

Only if walking access, admission conditions and travel times allow it. Discuss your priorities in advance if archaeology matters most: a busy day through the gorge includes several sites some distance apart.

On **day 7**, travelers explore the [Quebrada de Humahuaca](/argentina/place/quebrada-de-humahuaca/). The same day's route lists [Purmamarca](/argentina/place/purmamarca/), [Tilcara](/argentina/place/tilcara/), [Uquía](/argentina/place/uquia/), the [town of Humahuaca](/argentina/place/humahuaca/) and Inca Cueva. It is useful to distinguish **a stop on an itinerary** from a dedicated hiking excursion. The tour text confirms Inca Cueva as a stop but does not separately specify the walking distance to each rock shelter, time at an individual cave or exactly which areas are open. These details matter when estimating physical effort and must match the version of the day's route selected.

Travelers wanting more time for the rock paintings should distinguish a busy overview of Jujuy from a dedicated archaeological outing. The former covers several settlements and landscapes in one day; the latter puts the walk to the site and on-site exploration first.

## Why Inca Cueva Belongs on a Jujuy Journey

Northwestern Argentina combines archaeology with striking geography. In Purmamarca, travelers admire multicolored hillsides. Tilcara introduces the culture and history of the gorge's inhabitants. Uquía and Humahuaca reveal settlements linked to a historic route through the Andes. Inca Cueva adds ancient rock paintings to that sequence.

The images date from different periods of human presence. Although the site's name refers to the Incas, its archaeological history reaches much further back. Specialists in Jujuy conduct research into painting techniques and the condition of cave images. The rock surfaces therefore need careful treatment: view the paintings from a suitable distance and follow guides' instructions.

The [Quebrada de Humahuaca](/argentina/place/quebrada-de-humahuaca/) is also a UNESCO-listed cultural landscape. However, the World Heritage status of the valley as a whole should not be attributed automatically to each individual shelter or archaeological site within it. The geographical and historical context is what matters to understanding the itinerary.

## Preparing to Visit the Rock Shelters

Inca Cueva's main characteristics are **a dry, high-altitude environment and a possible walking approach**. The site is north of Humahuaca town. Individual rock shelters are reached on foot across stony terrain; the nature of the walk depends on which area and visiting format are chosen. If you specifically want to see a particular cave, agree on the time needed and whether a walk is required when planning the day's activities.

Closed shoes with good grip, water, a hat and sun protection are useful. A sunny day in the Jujuy mountains may be warm, while wind and evening temperatures can be considerably cooler. Take an extra layer even if the forecast is clear.

Another practical consideration is **altitude above sea level**. The tour includes regions with very different climates, and northern Argentina reaches much higher elevations than coastal cities. On a walk, a steady pace is better than attempting to fit every stop into the shortest possible time. If you are sensitive to altitude, plan according to how you feel.

## Comparing Inca Cueva with Other Stops

| Site | Main experience |
|---|---|
| [Inca Cueva](/argentina/place/inca-cueva/) | Rock paintings and shelters |
| [Purmamarca](/argentina/place/purmamarca/) | Colorful hillsides and mountain settlement |
| [Tilcara](/argentina/place/tilcara/) | History and culture of the gorge |
| [Salinas Grandes](/argentina/place/salinas-grandes/) | Vast salt flat and open plateau |

These are different reasons to visit Jujuy. For archaeology, Inca Cueva and the gorge's historic sites offer the most to explore. For colorful mountains, broad landscapes and photography, Purmamarca and the Salinas Grandes salt flat are more rewarding. The [15-day journey through Argentina and Iguazu](/multi-country/tour/argentina-grand-tour-15-days/) combines these experiences in one northern stage without requiring a separate trip for just one monument.

For a wider itinerary, compare [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/) and [cultural and historical journeys involving Argentina](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/argentina/). The thematic selection includes programs in which Argentina plays different roles, so check each tour's main stops.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Tours Visiting Inca Cueva

### Does Ada Tours have a journey including Inca Cueva on its main route?

Yes. The [15-day grand tour of Argentina](/multi-country/tour/argentina-grand-tour-15-days/) includes Inca Cueva on the Quebrada de Humahuaca day, alongside Purmamarca, Tilcara, Uquía and Humahuaca town.

### How many days are dedicated to Inca Cueva itself?

There is no separate full day exclusively for this site. It forms part of a busy **seventh day** with several stops in northern Argentina. The tour does not specify the duration of a visit to an individual cave.

### Does this journey stay entirely in Argentina?

No. Most of the journey explores regions of Argentina, but the itinerary also visits **the Brazilian side of Iguazu Falls**. It combines cultural, natural and gastronomic experiences.

### Can a busy sightseeing day be replaced with a detailed cave visit?

That change would require separate agreement on the program and logistics. The existing tour confirms an Inca Cueva stop but does not promise a separate extended archaeological trek.

### Is this stop suitable without hiking experience?

A potential walking section and the elevation need assessment. The difficulty depends on the available route to the rock shelters, so decide in advance which caves are planned and how much walking they require.

## What to See in Argentina: Cities, the Andes, Glaciers and Patagonia

Argentina is best explored through several distinct journeys. [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) offers urban culture, [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) offers wineries and Andean views, [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) offers glaciers, and [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) opens the way to Tierra del Fuego. Even within one country, each region requires its own logistics.

Here you will find {{catalog.placesCountPhrase}} to help select destinations according to regional differences. Check actual dates, hotels, services and excursions in the [Argentina tours catalog](/argentina/tour/), where the specific contents of each itinerary matter.

## Buenos Aires: Where to Start

[Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) is a city of neighborhoods with distinct architecture and cultures. La Boca and San Telmo offer historic streets, the Plaza de Mayo area is connected with Argentina's political history, while theaters and tango provide evening experiences.

One sightseeing day offers an initial impression, but allow more time for museums, exploring several neighborhoods and an outing to the Tigre Delta. The capital deserves its own place in the itinerary rather than serving only as an airport stop before Patagonia.

## Mendoza and Western Argentina: Vineyards Beside the Andes

[Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) is known for its wineries and gastronomy. In the city, you can walk through central squares and San Martín Park; the main wine program requires trips to individual estates. The sequence of visits depends on winery locations, reservations and the tasting format chosen.

The same part of western Argentina includes Andean mountain areas, but visits to high-altitude locations involve a very different level of physical exertion. [Aconcagua](/argentina/place/aconcagua/) is a landmark for mountain travel. Visiting accessible viewpoints and climbing to the summit are not the same: mountaineering requires specialist preparation and separate arrangements. Mentioning Aconcagua in an itinerary's geography does not mean an ascent is included.

For gastronomy enthusiasts, it is better to compare [wine journeys](/interests/food-and-wine/) with general multi-region tours than to squeeze a winery visit between two long flights.

## El Calafate and Perito Moreno: Glacial Patagonia

[El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) is a major starting point for visits to [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) in Los Glaciares National Park. The usual introductory experience is a visit to specially designed walkways and viewing platforms. Boat trips and specialized ice treks are possible on some programs, subject to their own requirements.

Even when the forecast is good, Patagonia's wind, sudden weather changes and travel time to natural attractions must be considered. The glacier and town serve different purposes: the glacier is the natural attraction, while the town provides accommodation and a base for excursions.

## El Chaltén: Mountain Trails and Time for Weather

[El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/) attracts hikers seeking the mountain landscapes of southern Patagonia. The length, elevation gain and difficulty of the selected trail, along with the weather forecast, matter particularly here. An extra day can be more valuable than attempting several demanding hikes in a row.

Combining El Calafate and El Chaltén makes geographical sense, but they offer different activities: glaciers are seen from viewing paths or on excursions, while mountain trails require independent physical effort or suitable guided arrangements. [Adventure tours in Argentina](/interests/adventure/tours/argentina/) are available where appropriate itineraries are listed in the current catalog.

## Ushuaia and Tierra del Fuego: The Beagle Channel and Southern Landscapes

[Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) lies beside the Beagle Channel. From here, visitors explore Tierra del Fuego National Park, coastal landscapes and the archipelago's natural environment. Boat trips and hikes depend on the weather and the selected program.

Ushuaia is also important for some expedition routes to Antarctica, but visiting the city does not itself include an expedition. Such trips must be compared separately by dates, vessel, route and conditions.

## Northwest and Lake District: Other Sides of Argentina

[Salta](/argentina/place/salta/) suits travelers interested in northwestern landscapes, culture and routes through valleys. [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/) lies in the lake-and-mountain district of northern Patagonia, providing a different experience from the south's glacial region.

Either region could be the main purpose of a separate journey. Including Salta and southern Patagonia in one route makes sense only with the large distances and additional domestic flights taken into account.

## Choosing Regions and Seasons

| Interest | Where to focus |
|---|---|
| Tango and city life | Buenos Aires |
| Wine and gastronomy | Mendoza |
| Glaciers | El Calafate |
| Mountain hiking | El Chaltén |
| Tierra del Fuego | Ushuaia |
| Lakes and mountains | Bariloche |

Argentina's southern-hemisphere summer runs from December to February, but elevation and latitude create very different conditions across regions. Even in warmer months, glaciers and mountains in Patagonia call for layers and wind protection. For Mendoza and the northwest, check the weather of the exact area you are visiting. Allow extra time for transport connections when traveling between several regions.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Argentina's Attractions

### Which places are best for a first trip to Argentina?

Combining [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) with one additional region is often sensible: [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) for wine or [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) for glaciers. The choice depends on trip duration and season.

### Can I see glaciers and Tierra del Fuego on one trip?

Yes, both can feature in a multi-stop journey, but transport and spare time between [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) and [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) must be planned in advance. Check the actual sequence in the chosen tour.

### Are Perito Moreno and El Chaltén the same place?

No. [Perito Moreno](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) is a glacier visited from the El Calafate region, while [El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/) is a base for mountain hiking. The physical demands and visiting arrangements differ.

### Where can I find cultural and gastronomic programs?

For individual destinations, start with [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/), then compare available [excursions](/argentina/excursion/) and [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/) by their actual contents.

## Ischigualasto: The Valley of the Moon and Argentina's Ancient History

Ischigualasto is a provincial natural park in northeastern San Juan province, Argentina, known as *Valle de la Luna*, the Valley of the Moon. The desert landscape exposes colorful rock layers and formations named after familiar shapes: a mushroom, a submarine and balls.

The park's scientific value goes far beyond its unusual scenery. Scientists study fossil plants and animals from the Triassic period in these rocks, when early dinosaurs appeared and the ancestors of mammals evolved. Together with neighboring [Talampaya National Park](/argentina/place/talampaya-national-park/), Ischigualasto forms a UNESCO World Heritage property.

## Why Ischigualasto Matters to Paleontology

The rocks of the Valley of the Moon preserve exceptionally detailed evidence of life on land during the Triassic period, approximately 250–200 million years ago. Different geological formations are exposed across the two neighboring parks, allowing researchers to reconstruct changes in plants, animals and ancient environments.

This is why Ischigualasto interests more than dinosaur enthusiasts. The site shows how scientists learn about vertebrate evolution from layers of sedimentary rock. Alongside paleontological finds are cliffs sculpted by erosion in much more recent periods. A rock shape visible in a photograph and the age of a fossil do not necessarily represent the same geological event.

Ischigualasto protects scientific discoveries. Visitors should not leave permitted routes in search of fossils or take away stones and rock fragments.

## What Will You See on the Valley of the Moon Route?

### El Hongo and Other Rock Formations

El Hongo ("The Mushroom") is one of the most recognizable silhouettes: a relatively narrow base supports a wider top. Visitors also see El Submarino ("The Submarine"), Cancha de Bochas ("Bowling Court"), Valle Pintado and other stops on the official route.

These formations were created by long-term natural processes acting on rocks of different resistance. Free movement among them is restricted by park rules, and visitors follow a designated excursion route through the protected landscape.

### Colored Strata and Open Desert

Along the route, you can see gray, ocher, reddish and other shades of rock. Their combination and striking forms create the celebrated lunar landscape. In the dry air and open terrain, shadows are especially noticeable as they change throughout the day.

The regular sightseeing circuit is by vehicle with an authorized guide. The park's official tourism description gives approximately 42 kilometers and around 3 hours for the standard circuit, but the precise route, accessible stops and duration should be confirmed for your travel date.

## How Ischigualasto Differs from Talampaya

Both parks belong to the same UNESCO natural World Heritage property, but lie in different provinces. Ischigualasto in San Juan is known for exposed multicolored rocks and individual formations on a plateau. [Talampaya in La Rioja](/argentina/place/talampaya-national-park/) is remembered for towering red canyon walls and routes along a dry watercourse.

Your main interest helps determine which to visit. Ischigualasto is well suited to learning about early dinosaurs and Triassic deposits. Talampaya offers major canyons and rock art from other eras. If your route allows both, the experiences complement each other.

## Getting There and Planning an Overnight Stay

The main tourist base near Ischigualasto is the San Agustín del Valle Fértil area. From [San Juan](/argentina/place/san-juan/), driving to the natural area takes a substantial part of the day, so the park is rarely worth trying to fit in as a short stop between city appointments.

For journeys through western Argentina, it makes sense to reach Valle Fértil first, allow a dedicated period for the official Ischigualasto circuit, and visit Talampaya the following day. Consider driving time to the entrance and the start of organized excursions rather than distances on the map alone.

## Ischigualasto in a Current Ada Tours Itinerary

On our ["Argentina: Journey into the Prehistoric World"](/argentina/tour/argentina-prehistoric-journey/) route, you travel from San Juan to Valle Fértil and visit Ischigualasto in the afternoon. On the following day, participants continue to Talampaya.

The geological parks are therefore not combined into one uninterrupted excursion: each has its own stop in the sequence of a longer journey that also includes other parts of Argentina.

## When to Go and How to Prepare

The park has an open, dry landscape with strong sunlight, little shade and noticeable temperature changes. Bring water, a hat, sun protection, closed shoes and an extra clothing layer for a cool morning or evening.

Bad weather and strong winds may affect permitted visits. Check the park's timetable and entry arrangements before setting off. Ticket prices, hours and route access depend on current rules, not on historic descriptions of a trip.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Ischigualasto

### Why is it called the Valley of the Moon?

Because of the exposed desert and unusual rock formations resembling an otherworldly landscape. Its scientific fame, however, comes from Triassic fossils.

### Can Ischigualasto be visited without a guide?

The main vehicle-based sightseeing route requires accompaniment by a park guide. Check official information for current entry procedures and other visiting options.

### Are Talampaya and Ischigualasto the same park?

No. They are two separate protected areas in neighboring San Juan and La Rioja provinces, jointly recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage property.

It links the capital, wine-growing regions near the Andes, two famous geological parks and Patagonia's Atlantic coast. {{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_argentina_puteshestvie_v_doistoricheskij_mir}}

## Which Tour Days Are Devoted to the Valley of the Moon and Talampaya?

**Day 6. Mendoza – San Juan.** After time in [Mendoza's](/argentina/place/mendoza/) wine region, travelers take a bus to [San Juan](/argentina/place/san-juan/), transfer and explore the city. This marks a transition from Andean vineyards to the drier landscapes of central-western Argentina.

**Day 7. Ischigualasto.** After breakfast, the route heads from San Juan toward Valle Fértil. In the afternoon, travelers visit the Valley of the Moon, tour the park and return to the hotel for dinner. **Breakfast and dinner** are included on this day. Ischigualasto is a confirmed itinerary stop, not merely an optional excursion on offer.

**Day 8. [Talampaya](/argentina/place/talampaya-national-park/).** The next day takes travelers to neighboring La Rioja province. Towering red canyon walls, ancient landscapes and semi-desert conditions define this experience. After the excursion, the itinerary returns toward San Juan. Breakfast is included on this day.

The sequence makes the journey worthwhile: **two protected areas are visited on consecutive days**, offering both the multicolored strata of the Valley of the Moon and Talampaya's canyons. Treating the two parks as one stop would be inaccurate. They are in different provinces and offer distinct experiences.

## What Makes Ischigualasto Special: The Valley of the Moon and the Triassic

Ischigualasto and Talampaya form one UNESCO World Heritage property, **"Ischigualasto / Talampaya Natural Parks,"** inscribed in 2000. Its importance lies chiefly in the exceptionally complete geological record of the Triassic period, approximately **250–200 million years ago**. The deposits help scientists study the early evolution of dinosaurs, mammalian ancestors and ancient ecosystems.

For travelers, the geology is visible in the landscape itself. There are rounded boulders, eroded slopes and individually named rock formations. One of the most recognizable is **El Hongo**, a mushroom-shaped rock. Daylight changes the colors of the desert surfaces, making the stone landscape particularly rewarding when observed at an unhurried pace from the route's stops.

Despite its name, this is neither the lunar surface nor a volcanic landscape. Its appearance comes from Earth processes: sediment deposition, crustal movement and prolonged weathering. Paleontological discoveries give another reason to protect the area and remain on designated visitor routes.

## Ischigualasto or Talampaya: What's the Difference?

| Site | Main attraction |
|---|---|
| [Ischigualasto](/argentina/place/ischigualasto/) | Triassic rocks, formations and Valley of the Moon |
| [Talampaya](/argentina/place/talampaya-national-park/) | Red canyon walls and desert gorges |

At Ischigualasto, attention often falls on rock colors and textures, formations and accounts of ancient life. At Talampaya, the scenery feels different: major canyons and high rock walls dominate the landscape. Both parks are known for paleontological material, but **one cannot replace the other**.

On the [13-day Argentina journey](/argentina/tour/argentina-prehistoric-journey/), comparing them is easy because they are visited on consecutive days. If you only have time for one park while traveling independently, choose based on its location in your route and the landscape you want, not simply the most striking photographs.

## How the Park Visit Works and What to Prepare

San Juan province's official tourism portal describes Ischigualasto's main vehicle-based circuit as **a route accompanied by a park guide**. The visit follows established stops within the protected area; unrestricted independent driving off-route is not the normal format. The park also offers special routes beyond the usual daytime circuit, but their existence does not mean they are included in the Ada Tours itinerary.

The climate is dry, the summer sun intense, and temperature and wind can quickly change how comfortable it feels. Bring drinking water, closed shoes, sun protection, lightweight clothing and an extra layer if it gets cool. Driving times between cities and through the park depend on roads and the official visiting arrangements.

Check current park hours and restrictions before departure, as they change by season. **The price of an individual entrance ticket and participation rules should not be inferred from the basic price of the entire 13-day tour.** The program's inclusions determine what Ada Tours has paid for.

For this itinerary, the key point is that the Valley of the Moon is scheduled for **day seven**, and Talampaya for day eight. Rather than trying to fit both parks into one day, participants should plan their energy for two substantial excursions in succession.

## Who Will Enjoy This Combination of Natural Regions?

This route particularly appeals to travelers who want to discover Argentina beyond its best-known cities. It begins in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and the wine-growing areas of the [Uco Valley](/argentina/place/uco-valley/), before focusing on San Juan, Ischigualasto and Talampaya. The next major stage visits [Puerto Madryn](/argentina/place/puerto-madryn/) and the [Valdés Peninsula](/argentina/place/valdes-peninsula/), where Atlantic wildlife becomes the main attraction.

The combination suits people equally interested in Earth's history, landscapes and living nature. For a short trip solely to San Juan, the 13-day program would be too extensive, as much of it visits other regions. For a first broad exploration of Argentina, the connections between natural areas are a major advantage.

Other options are in the [Argentina tours catalog](/argentina/tour/), while [Argentina nature itineraries](/interests/wildlife/tours/argentina/) offer different combinations of parks and landscapes.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Ischigualasto Tours

### On which day is the Valley of the Moon scheduled?

In the [13-day Argentina tour](/argentina/tour/argentina-prehistoric-journey/), Ischigualasto is visited **on day seven**, after the journey from San Juan to Valle Fértil. Dinner is planned after returning from the excursion.

### Does the same tour also include Talampaya?

Yes. [Talampaya National Park](/argentina/place/talampaya-national-park/) is on the following, eighth day. It is a separate excursion in neighboring La Rioja province.

### Is Ischigualasto an Argentine national park?

No. It is **a provincial park in San Juan**. Together with Talampaya National Park, it forms one UNESCO World Heritage property.

### Do we have to walk through the park?

The standard Ischigualasto tourist route is **by vehicle with compulsory guiding by a park guide** and stops for sightseeing. Special hikes and other activities are available separately and must be explicitly included in the chosen visiting format.

### Which is best for dinosaurs and geology?

Ischigualasto is particularly informative for Triassic deposits, while nearby Talampaya complements it with different scenery. The itinerary described visits both on consecutive days so you can see the differences.
